restatement: Add a Replay page at #/picks/<id>/replay that plays a pick's Decision log back one event at a time. Boyd should be able to scrub to any moment of Pick 4 and see, in under five seconds: how long the pick had been running (+2h 53m), its status chip (judging), its stage (Film Room), which runs were on the field and how each one ended so far, which stages were done and how long each took, and the sentence for what just happened, with its agent or pull-request link. Play steps through the film at one event per second, so the whole of Pick 4 plays in 19 seconds, which is the backbone of the demo video.

rubric.name: Frame fidelity on real logs
rubric.howToGrade: Your pooled R1-R4, R9, R12-R14. Then by hand in the harness: open p-20261017-93 at its fix-loop verdict (?at= that seq) and p-20261017-98 at its last frame and compare with the frame table; check one live prefix (timeline(events.slice(0, 12), …) of p-20261017-94) and one synthetic final stage (events.slice(0, 2) with now after the 48 h timeout). 4 = every frame of all five fixtures equals frameAt() and both by-hand cases are right. One wrong run state or stage duration on a real log = 2 at most. Any duration formatted in the browser (replay.js computing minutes or hours) = 1 at most.

rubric.name: Playback discipline
rubric.howToGrade: Your pooled R5-R8, R10, R11. Then by hand with the fake clock: Play, three live updates inside one step, then tick: one timer pending and the step lands on time; Pause during play and update twice: still paused; press Last event with focus on Next event: focus ends on the Event slider; leave to #/ while playing: zero timers. Any path that leaves two timers, a timer after leaving, or a lost place after an update = 1 at most.

rubric.name: Game-film screens
rubric.howToGrade: Run cdp-shot.mjs per label on #/picks/p-20261017-94/replay?at=1, ?at=11 and ?at=20 at 390×844, 430×932 and 1280×800, light and dark (18 runs), plus the pick page at 390×844 dark. 4 = every probe ok: true with exactly one chip of the frame's status, scrollWidth ≤ width, and from the ?at=11 390 dark and 1280 light screenshots you can say within 5 seconds the elapsed time, the status, what just happened and which runs are on the field. 3 = probes pass but one screen is cramped or a caption is truncated. 2 = one W7/W8/W9 problem left. 0 = the page scrolls sideways at 390 or a control is under 44×44 at 1280. Screenshots are required for a 3 or 4.

angles: Frame engine: start from the frame rule; write one pure function that maps (timeline, index) to a frame, row by row from the spec's frame table, one module-level playback record (pick id, index, playing, timer), and one paint function that updates persistent nodes in place; smallest app.js hunks; plain CSS that meets the size rules; tests drive every frame of every fixture through compareFrame.

Broadcast booth: start from the demo video; the film reads like a sports broadcast: a big scoreboard (clock, status chip, stage, counter), the caption as a lower third, and at 1280 px the runs as a field of lanes beside the film; on a phone the controls sit in one thumb-reach bar (safe-area aware) under the film; transitions only inside @media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference); tokens only, both schemes; paused on any 390 px dark screenshot, a stranger can say how long the pick has run, what just happened and who is still on the field.

Chapter cuts: start from the story; cut the film into chapters by stage: a Chapters nav outside the Replay controls group with one link or button per stage reached so far (each at least 44x44, never a .chip), jumping to that stage's first event, the current chapter marked; the fix loop in Pick 3 and the NOT_VERIFIED in Pick 4 are easy to find; accessible names and aria-valuetext read well in VoiceOver order (film, controls, chapters, lists); extra controls never break the playback rules or the probe.
forbidden: Draft PRs only. Never mark a PR ready for review, never merge, never enable auto-merge, never deploy or publish anything.
Candidates open no pull request at all (push your branch only). If your environment opens one automatically, it must be a draft with base dd/p4-phone, and say so in your report.
Touch only BoydVC/draft-day. Nothing KPD, kpdlawgroup, or debt-collection related, in code, fixtures, tests or examples.
Do not push to main, dd/scaffold, dd/p1-film-room*, dd/p2-timeline*, dd/p3-lessons* or dd/p4-phone*, and do not force-push.
Do not edit a file the touch map marks do-not-touch.

No runtime dependencies, no network code (the A15 guard in test/guards.test.ts stays as is), no secrets, no LLM calls, no web fonts or other-origin assets, no localStorage/sessionStorage/cookies/history writes.
